FILED s530b (Opus agent, 2026-10-31), from the Template-Toolkit re-census.  PRE-EXISTING (main 5faf9c8f and ff5f72b5 alike).  SILENT.

    my @k = qw(a b c); my @v = (1, 2); my %g; my $h = {};
    @g{ @k } = (@v, 3);          # perl a=1,b=2,c=3   PCL a=2,b=3,c=
    @$h{ @k } = (@v, 3);         # same
    @{$h}{ @k } = (('x') x 2, 'y');   # perl x,x,y  PCL 2,y,undef
    my @a; @a[0,1,2] = (@v, 3);  # perl 1 2 3  PCL 2 3 undef
perl: the right side is a LIST, flattened like every list assignment's.

CAUSE: the two slice arms of p-setf (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) read the right side through %p-slice-src-bindings, which coerced it to a vector and SNAPSHOTTED it, but never FLATTENED it: the emitter's `(vector @v 3)` arrives with the array itself as one element (a list assignment's p-list-= / p-array-= flatten it; the slice arms did not).

Template-Toolkit: Template/Grammar.pm fills its lexer table with `@$LEXTABLE{ @RESERVED, @cmpop, @binop, @tokens } = ( @RESERVED, ('CMPOP') x @cmpop, ('BINOP') x @binop, @tokens );` -- every reserved word mapped to "2", so `[% IF %]`, `[% BLOCK %]`, `[% INCLUDE %]`, `[% FOREACH %]` were parse errors ("unexpected token").

FIX (one mechanism): %p-slice-src-vector -- the all-scalar right side (the literal list, the common case: every element %p-flatten-sized-p) keeps the lazy %p-assign-snapshot-vector (no allocation); anything else goes through %p-flatten-list, the walk every list assignment uses (one FETCH per tied element).
GUARD: Pl/t/aassign-01.t (the slice rows; inverse-verified on main).
